newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares retrench, end electronic trade lower.
newsitem.headline: German shares retrench, end electronic trade lower.

text.p: German shares were generally lower in late dealings on Tuesday, with some at fresh session lows as traders said the market was trying to find its footing after recent advances to new all-time record levels.

The IBIS DAX index, which tracks electronic trade in 30 blue-chips, ended down 22.60 points, or 0.51 percent at 4,377.70 points, off earlier lows by still hurt by the weaker dollar and early losses on Wall Street.
The DAX index ended bourse trade up 10.53 points, or 0.24 percent, at 4,381.69 points.
Traders said they had expected the IBIS DAX to end dealings in minus territory but noted that the upward trend was still intact and that the market was in a consolidative tone.
"The pressure from America became too much," said one Frankfurt dealer. "They are lower, so we are lower too."
Dealers said a lack of fresh impulses kept the market on the defensive, while some said the DAX index was merely out of breath after rising as much as 615 points in July.
"We need to take a break," said one dealer. "We are not going to head much lower but we needed some consolidation."
A flood of corporate earnings results, particularly in the banking sector, gave the market fresh fundamentals during morning dealings to digest.

Dresdner Bank AG ended the day up 1.87 marks, or 2.28 percent, at 83.82 marks after saying it planned to raise its base capital by 120 million marks by issuing new shares and was keen to expand activities in the United States.
The bank, the second-largest in Germany, also said earnings were up 23 percent in the first half of the year.

Commerzbank AG, considered the next target after Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank said they will merge, ended bourse trade higher, but fell sharply in post-bourse dealings to end down 82 pfennigs at 60.99 marks.
Carmaker BMW AG slumped 57.50 marks, or 3.91 percent, to 1.412.50 marks despite reporting a first-half group net profit of 435 million marks.
The profit figure was viewed as being slightly above market expectations for about 400 million marks.
Dealers said other carmakers were benefiting from the positive outlook for the sector, which has been bolstered by the weak mark making exports more competitve.

Daimler-Benz AG, maker of Mercedes vehicles, ended 1.65 marks higher at 156.90 marks, off earlier highs, as traders set a near-term target of 160 marks. Daimler will release six-month results on Thursday.

Degussa AG, the metal and chemicals group, pared earlier gains to end 1.55 marks down at 103.10 marks. The shares rose earlier after the group reported a 10 percent rise in nine-month group sales to 11.2 billion marks.
Degussa also said it expected a higher profit for the 1996/97 year.

Among other shares posting notable losses over the day was sportswear group Puma AG, which ended down 2.50 marks, or 4.55 percent, at 52.50 marks amid fresh takeover talk for the Herzogenaurach-based group.
